## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Munikajātaka* (Ja 30) is a birth story belonging to the *Kuruṅgavagga* in the *Ekanipāta* of the Pali Jātaka collection [Fausböll 1877]. The narrative was delivered by the Buddha at the Jetavana monastery regarding a monk who had become discontented after being seduced by a plump young woman (*thullakumārikā*), an incident noted as structurally linked to the *Culla-Nārada-Kassapa-jātaka* of the *Terasakanipāta* [Fausböll 1877]. In the conclusion (*samodhāna*), the Buddha reveals that the discontented monk in a past life was the pig named Munika (*Munikasūkara*), the young woman was the plump maiden, Cullalohita was Ānanda, and the Bodhisatta was Mahālohita [Fausböll 1877].
